# An ideal times its conjugate is generated by its norm

Let $n\ge1$, $\mathcal O$ the ring of integers of $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $\sigma$ the
nontrivial automorphism. Every ideal $I$ of $\mathcal O$ satisfies
$$I\cdot\sigma(I)=\bigl(N(I)\bigr),$$
the principal ideal generated by the natural number $N(I)$. Consequently $N(\tau I)=N(I)$ for
every automorphism $\tau$ of $K$ and every ideal $I$.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the factorization of $I$ into prime ideals. For $I=0$ both sides
are $0$, and for $I=\mathcal O$ both are $\mathcal O$. For a nonzero prime $P$, lying over a prime
$p$, the trichotomy gives $P\cdot\sigma P=p\mathcal O=(N(P))$ when $P$ is split or ramified, and
$P\cdot\sigma P=P^2=p^2\mathcal O=(N(P))$ when it is inert. Both sides are multiplicative in $I$.
For the norms, the case $\tau=1$ is clear, and $N(I)=0$ means $I=0=\tau I$. Otherwise
$\tau=\sigma$ and $N(I)N(\sigma I)=N(N(I)\mathcal O)=N(I)^2$, and $N(I)\ne0$ can be cancelled.
